Warning: In this document, Gamma(α,β) refers to the p.d.f. ρ(x)=βαΓ(α)1​xα−1e−βx​1{x>0}​. This definition is same as the definition in Statistical Inference by George Casella, but may be different from many other books by Chinese authors. Therefore, conclusions regarding the Gamma distribution or the exponential distribution may differ by a reciprocal transformation of the second parameter β.

Problem 1.2

X1​∼Gamma(α1​,β), X2​∼Gamma(α2​,β), X1​ and X2​ are independent. Calculate the conditional distribution of X1​∣X1​+X2​=t for any t>0.

Solution: Since X1​∼Gamma(α1​,β),X2​∼Gamma(α2​,β), we know thatρX1​​(x1​)=βα1​Γ(α1​)1​x1α1​−1​e−βx1​​1(0,+∞)​(x1​),ρX2​​(x2​)=βα2​Γ(α2​)1​x2α2​−1​e−βx2​​1(0,+∞)​(x2​),thenρX1​,X2​​(x1​,x2​)=βα1​+α2​Γ(α1​)Γ(α2​)1​x1α1​−1​x2α2​−1​e−βx1​+x2​​1(0,+∞)​(x1​)1(0,+∞)​(x2​).

we know thatρX1​,X1​+X2​​(y1​,y2​)=ρX1​,X2​​(y1​,y2​−y1​)⋅1=βα1​+α2​Γ(α1​)Γ(α2​)y1α1​−1​(y2​−y1​)α2​−1​e−α2​y2​​1(y2​>y1​>0)​.

ThusρX1​∣X1​+X2​​(y1​∣y2​)=ρX1​+X2​​(y2​)ρX1​,X1​+X2​​(y1​,y2​)​=∫R​ρX1​,X1​+X2​​(y1​,y2​)dy1​ρX1​,X1​+X2​​(y1​,y2​)​=∫R​y1α1​−1​(y2​−y1​)α2​−11{y2​>y1​>0}​dy1​y1α1​−1​(y2​−y1​)α2​−11{y2​>y1​>0}​​=B(α1​,α2​)y2α1​+α2​−1​y1α1​−1​(y2​−y1​)α2​−11{y2​>y1​>0}​​.So, X1​∣X1​+X2​=t∼B(α1​,α2​)tα1​+α2​−1xα1​−1(t−x)α2​−1​1(0,t)​(x)dx.

Problem 1.5

Check (1) If X∼F(m,n), then 1/X∼F(n,m); (2) If X∼t(n), then X2∼F(1,n); (3) If X∼F(m,n), then 1+nm​Xm​∼Beta(2m​,2n​) (cf. Definition 1.6); (4) E(Gamma(α,β)1​)=(α−1)β1​ for α>1. Further, E(X2(n)1​)=n−21​ and E(F(m,n))=n−2n​ for n>2.

Solution: (1) X=χ2(n)/nχ2(m)/m​∼F(m,n)So,X1​=χ2(m)/mχ2(n)/n​∼F(n,m)(2)X=X2​/n​X1​​∼tn​,X1​∼N(0,1),X2​∼χ2(n)X2=X2​/nX12​​∼F(1,n),where X12​∼χ2(1).

(3) LetX=Y/nZ/m​,Z∼χ2(m),Y∼χ2(n)then 1+nm​Xm​=Z+YZ​. Let’s consider a general transform forU=Z+Y,V=Z+YZ​where Z∼Gamma(α1​,β) and Y∼Gamma(α2​,β), Z and Y are independent. Note Gamma(2n​,2)=χ2(n)(Z,Y)∼Γ(α1​)Γ(α2​)βα1​+α2​1​zα1​−1yα2​−1e−βz​e−βy​,z>0,y>0.

Therefore,(U,V)∼Γ(α1​)Γ(α2​)βα1​+α2​1​(uv)α1​−1[u(1−v)]α2​−1ue−βu​=Γ(α1​+α2​)βα1​+α2​1​uα1​+α2​−1e−βu​Γ(α1​)Γ(α2​)Γ(α1​+α2​)​vα1​−1(1−v)α2​−1Further, we haveU∼Gamma(α1​+α2​,β) and V∼Beta(α1​,α2​),and U and V are independent. Particularly, 1+nm​Xm​∼Beta(2m​,2n​).

(4)E(Gamma(α,β)1​)=βαΓ(α)1​∫0∞​x1​xα−1e−βx​dx=Γ(α)Γ(α−1)​β1​=β(α−1)1​χ2 distribution is Gamma(2n​,2), so,E(χ2(n)1​)=n−21​E(F(m,n))=E(X/nY/m​)=mn​E(Y)E(X1​)=mn​×m×n−21​=n−2n​

Problem 1.8

X∣λ∼ Poisson(λ) and λ∼ Gamma(α,β), derive the distribution of X. (It is a negative binomial if α is an integer.)

Solution: The pmf of X, for x=0,1,…, isfX​(x)=∫0∞​fX​(x∣λ)fΛ​(λ)dλ=∫0∞​x!λxe−λ​Γ(α)βα1​λα−1e−λ/βdλ=x!Γ(α)βα1​∫0∞​λ(x+α)−1exp⎩⎨⎧​−(1+ββ​)λ​⎭⎬⎫​dλ=x!Γ(α)βα1​Γ(x+α)(1+ββ​)x+α=x!Γ(α)Γ(x+α)​(1+ββ​)x(1+β1​)α.

Problem 1.9

Further, X∣N∼Binomial(N,p), N∼Poisson(Λ), and Λ∼Gamma(α,β), find the marginal distribution of X. (three-stage model) (hint: derive X∣Λ∼Poisson(Λp) first)

Solution: For x=0,1,…, we haveP(X=x∣λ)=n=x∑∞​P(X=x∣N=n,λ)P(N=n∣λ)=n=x∑∞​(xn​)px(1−p)n−xn!e−λλn​=n=x∑∞​x!(n−x)!1​(1−pp​)x[(1−p)λ]ne−λ=e−λm=0∑∞​x!m!1​(1−pp​)x[(1−p)λ]m+x(let m=n−x)=x!1​e−λ(1−pp​)x[(1−p)λ]xm=0∑∞​m![(1−p)λ]m​=x!e−λ(pλ)xe(1−p)λ​=x!(pλ)xe−pλ​,i.e. the Poisson(pλ) pmf. Thus X∣Λ∼Poisson(pλ). Now calculations like those in Problem 1.8 yield the pmf of X, for x=0,1,…, isfX​(x)=Γ(α)x!(pβ)α1​Γ(x+α)(1+pβpβ​)x+α=x!(α+x−1)(α+x−2)⋯(α+1)α​(1+pβpβ​)x(1+pβ1​)α.

Problem 1.10

If X∣μ∼N(μ,σ12​) and μ∼N(δ,σ22​), check X∼N(δ,σ12​+σ22​) and μ∣X∼N(σ12​+σ22​σ12​​δ+σ12​+σ22​σ22​​X,σ12​+σ22​σ12​σ22​​). So the mean of posterior distribution, i.e. Bayes estimator of μ, is a weighted sum of prior mean and X.

Solution: (1)E(etX∣μ)=eμt+21​σ12​t2,E(eμt)=eδt+21​σ22​t2E(etX)=E(E(etX∣μ))=E(eμt⋅e21​σ12​t2)=e21​σ12​t2⋅E(eμt)=eδt+21​(σ12​+σ22​)t2,so X∼N(δ,σ12​+σ22​).

(2)f(μ∣X)=f(X)f(X,μ)​=2π(σ12​+σ22​)​1​e−2(σ12​+σ22​)(X−δ)2​2π​σ1​1​e−2σ12​(X−μ)2​2π​σ2​1​e−2σ22​(μ−δ)2​​=2π​σ12​+σ22​σ12​σ22​​​1​⋅exp⎣⎡​−2σ12​+σ22​σ12​σ22​​[μ−σ12​+σ22​σ12​​δ−σ12​+σ22​σ22​​X]2​⎦⎤​Therefore,μ∣X∼N(σ12​+σ22​σ12​​δ+σ12​+σ22​σ22​​X,σ12​+σ22​σ12​σ22​​).

Problem 1.11

Part I:

For any two r.v.s X and Y with finite variances, prove that

(a) Cov(X,Y)=Cov(X,E(Y∣X));

(b) X and Y−E(Y∣X) are uncorrelated;

(c) Var(Y−E(Y∣X))=E(Var(Y∣X)).

Part II:

For any three r.v.s X, Y, and Z with finite variances, prove the covariance identityCov(X,Y)=E(Cov(X,Y∣Z))+Cov(E(X∣Z),E(Y∣Z)),where Cov(X,Y∣Z) is the covariance of X and Y under the pdf f(x,y∣z).

Solution: (a) First, E[XE(Y∣X)]=E[E(XY∣X)]=E(XY)Cov(X,E(Y∣X))=E[XE(Y∣X)]−EX⋅E[E(Y∣X)]=E(XY)−EX⋅EY=Cov(X,Y).

(b)Cov(X,Y−E(Y∣X))=E[XY−XE(Y∣X)]−EX⋅E[Y−E(Y∣X)]=E(XY)−E(XY)−EX(EY−EY)=0.

(c)Var(Y−E(Y∣X))=E(Y−E(Y∣X))2−[E(Y−E(Y∣X))]2=E[Y2+E2(Y∣X)−2YE(Y∣X)]=EY2+E[E2(Y∣X)]−2E[YE(Y∣X)]Note that E[YE(Y∣X)]=E[E[YE(Y∣X)∣X]]=E[E(Y∣X)E(Y∣X)], soVar[Y−E(Y∣X)]=EY2−E[E2(Y∣X)].As for E(Var(Y∣X))=E(E(Y2∣X)−E2(Y∣X))=EY2−E[E2(Y∣X)],

we have Var(Y−E(Y∣X))=E(Var(Y∣X)).

Part II:

Cov(X,Y)=E(XY)−E(X)E(Y)=E(E(XY∣Z))−E(E(X∣Z))E(E(Y∣Z))=E(E(XY∣Z))−E[E(X∣Z)E(Y∣Z)]+E[E(X∣Z)E(Y∣Z)]−E(E(X∣Z))E(E(Y∣Z))=E[E(XY∣Z)−E(X∣Z)E(Y∣Z)]+E[E(X∣Z)E(Y∣Z)]−E(E(X∣Z))E(E(Y∣Z))=E(Cov(X,Y∣Z))+Cov(E(X∣Z),E(Y∣Z)).

Problem 1.12

Assumption as in the previous “Property”, prove that ES≤σ, and if σ2>0, then ES<σ.

Proof. X1​,…,Xn​∼i.i.d.(μ,σ2).

Sn2​=n−11​(i=1∑n​Xi2​−nXˉ2)E(Sn2​)=n−11​(i=1∑n​E(Xi2​)−nE(Xˉ2))First we calculate E(Xˉ2).E(Xˉ2)=n21​E(i=1∑n​Xi​)2=n1​E(X12​)+nn−1​μ2=nσ2​+μ2.So we derive that E(Sn2​)=σ2. With Jensen inequality: given a convex function g, we have g(EX)≤E(g(X)). Take g(x)=x2, we can conclude that (E(Sn​))2≤E(Sn2​), thusE(Sn​)≤σ.Further, if σ>0, then P(Sn​=E(Sn​))=0. Note that g(x)=x2 is a strictly convex function, (E(Sn​))2<E(Sn2​), thus E(Sn​)<σ.

(1) Show that S2=2n(n−1)1​∑i=1n​∑j=1n​(Xi​−Xj​)2. Assume now that the X1​ has a finite fourth moment, and denote θ1​=EX1​, θj​=E(X1​−θ1​)j, j=2,3,4.

(2) Show that Var(S2)=n1​(θ4​−n−1n−3​θ22​).

(3) Find Cov(Xˉ,S2) in terms of θ1​,θ2​,θ3​, and θ4​. Under what conditions is Cov(Xˉ,S2)=0?

Solution: (1)2n(n−1)1​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​(Xi​−Xj​)2=2n(n−1)1​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​(Xi2​+Xj2​−2Xi​Xj​)=2n(n−1)1​[i=1∑n​2nXi2​−2i=1∑n​Xi​j=1∑n​Xj​]=n−11​(i=1∑n​Xi2​−nXˉ2)andS2​=n−11​i=1∑n​(Xi​−Xˉ)2=n−11​(i=1∑n​Xi2​−2nXˉ2+nXˉ2)=n−11​(i=1∑n​Xi2​−nXˉ2),​soS2=2n(n−1)1​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​(Xi​−Xj​)2.

(2)E(S2)​=2n(n−1)1​i∑​j∑​E(Xi​−Xj​)2=2n(n−1)1​(n2−n)E(X1​−X2​)2=Var(X1​)=σ2.​Var(S2)=E((S2)2)−σ4, where(S2)2​=4n2(n−1)21​(∑(Xi​−Xj​)2)2=4n2(n−1)21​i=j∑​(Xi​−Xj​)2k=l∑​(Xk​−Xl​)2=4n2(n−1)21​4i<j∑​(Xi​−Xj​)2k<l∑​(Xk​−Xl​)2=(i<j)&(k<l)∑​4n2(n−1)21​4(Xi​−Xj​)2(Xk​−Xl​)2.​We discuss the six following situations of (i,j),(k,l). Since each term is the addition and subtraction of random variables, let X~i​=Xi​−μ, we assume that each Xi​ has been centralized, i.e. E(Xi​)=0,∀i,1≤i≤n.

case (1): (i,j)≡(k,l),E(Xi​−Xj​)4=2θ4​+6θ22​;

case (2): k=i,j=l, i.e. (i,j)&(i,l)E[(Xi​−Xj​)2(Xi​−Xl​)2]=θ4​+3θ22​;

case (3): l=j,i=k, i.e. (i,j)&(k,j)E[(Xi​−Xj​)2(Xk​−Xj​)2]=θ4​+3θ22​;

case (4): i=l,j=k, i.e. (i,j)&(k,i)E[(Xi​−Xj​)2(Xk​−Xi​)2]=θ4​+3θ22​;

case (5): j=k,i=l, i.e. (i,j)&(j,l)E[(Xi​−Xj​)2(Xj​−Xl​)2]=θ4​+3θ22​;

case (6): i=k,j=l, i.e. (i,j)&(k,l)E[(Xi​−Xj​)2(Xk​−Xl​)2]=4θ22​.

Calculate solvability (number) of cases (1)-(6),

case (1): (2n​);

case (3): 3n(n−1)(n−2)​;

case (4): 21​3n(n−1)(n−2)​;

case (5): 21​3n(n−1)(n−2)​;

ThenVar(S2)=n1​[θ4​+n−1θ22​​(n2−2n+3)−nθ22​]=n1​[θ4​−n−1n−3​θ22​].

(3) We assume Xi​=Xi​−E(Xi​),Cov(Xˉ,S2)​=n1​nCov(X1​,S2)=Cov(X1​,S2)=2n(n−1)1​[Cov(X1​,(X1​−X2​)2)+⋯+Cov(X1​,(X1​−Xn​)2)]=n1​Cov(X1​,(X1​−X2​)2)=n1​Cov(X1​,X12​−2X1​X2​+X22​)=n1​[Cov(X1​,X12​)−2Cov(X1​,X1​X2​)],​andCov(X1​,X12​)Cov(X1​,2X1​X2​)​=E(X13​)−EX1​E(X12​)=θ3​,=E(X12​X2​)−0=0.​So, Cov(Xˉ,S2)=n1​θ3​ and if θ3​=0, we have Cov(Xˉ,S2)=0.

maxβ12​+β22​+…+βn2​=1​Var(β1​X1​+β2​X2​+…+βn​Xn​).

Solution: (1)Σ=(σ11​σ21​​σ12​σ22​​),Σ−1=∣Σ∣1​(σ22​−σ21​​−σ12​σ11​​)ρX1​X2​​=Var(X1​)Var(X2​)​Cov(X1​,X2​)​=σ11​σ22​​σ12​​=∣Σ∣σ22​∣Σ∣σ11​−∣Σ∣σ12​=σ11σ22​−σ12​.

(2)β=(β1​,…,βn​)⊤,β⊤β=1max​Var(β⊤X)=β⊤β=1max​β⊤Σβ.Let L(β,λ)=β⊤Σβ−λ(β⊤β−1),∂β∂L​=2Σβ−2λβ=0⇒Σβ=λβ,β⊤Σβ=β⊤λβ=λ.Therefore, maxβ⊤β=1​Var(β⊤X)=λ1​ (the maximum eigenvalue of Σ).

(3) Let β=(1,−β2​,…,−βn​)⊤, thenminVar(X1​−β2​X2​−…−βn​Xn​)⇔minβ⊤Σβ s.t. β⊤⎝⎛​10⋮0​⎠⎞​=1.Let L(β,λ)=β⊤Σβ−λ(β1​−1),⎩⎨⎧​∂β∂L​=2Σβ−λ⎝⎛​10⋮0​⎠⎞​=0⇒β=2λ​Σ−1⎝⎛​10⋮0​⎠⎞​=2λ​⎝⎛​θ11​θ12​⋮θ1n​​⎠⎞​∂λ∂L​=0⇒β1​=1,λ=θ11​2​​Therefore, βi​=−θ11​θ1i​​, i=2,…,n.

(4) Let Y=(X3​,…,Xn​), and partitionΣ=(Σ11​Σ21​​Σ12​Σ22​​),Σ11​=(σ11​σ21​​σ12​σ22​​)2×2​.Then(X1​,X2​)∣Y∼N(∗, Σ11​−Σ12​Σ22−1​Σ21​≜A2×2​),A=(a11​a21​​a12​a22​​).X1​⊥⊥X2​∣Y⇔a12​=0⇔ the (1,2) entry of A−1 is zero. Note thatΘ=((Σ11​−Σ12​Σ22−1​Σ21​)−1∗​∗∗​),so θ1,2​ is the (1,2) entry of A−1. Hence X1​⊥⊥X2​∣Y⇔θ1,2​=0.

Chapter 2Sample, Statistics and Distribution

Problem 2.1

Population U[0,1], order statistics U(1)​≤U(2)​≤…≤U(n)​. Check

(1) Joint pdf: f(u1​,…,un​)=n!1{0<u1​<u2​<⋯<un​<1}​

(2) U(k)​∼Beta(k,n−k+1)

(3) U(i+k)​−U(i)​∼Beta(k,n−k+1) independent of i

(4) Range U(n)​−U(1)​∼Beta(n−1,2)

Solution: (1) Easy.

(2)ρU(k)​​(x)=(k−1)!(n−k)!n!​xk−1(1−x)n−k1[0,1]​(x).SoρU(k)​​(x)​=(k−1)!(n−k)!n!​xk−1(1−x)n−k1[0,1]​(x)=Γ(k)Γ(n−k+1)Γ(n+1)​xk−1(1−x)n−k+1−11[0,1]​(x)=B(k,n−k+1)xk−1(1−x)n−k+1−1​1[0,1]​(x).​Hence U(k)​∼Beta(k,n−k+1).

(3)ρ(U(i)​,U(i+k)​)​(x,y)=(i−1)!(k−1)!(n−i−k)!n!​xi−1(y−x)k−1(1−y)n−i−k1{0≤x<y≤1}​.Thereforeρ(U(i+k)​−U(i)​,U(i)​)​(z,w)=ρ(U(i)​,U(i+k)​)​(w,z+w)⋅1=(i−1)!(k−1)!(n−i−k)!n!​wi−1zk−1(1−z−w)n−i−k1{w≥0,z≥0,w+z≤1}​.HenceρU(i+k)​−U(i)​​(z)=∫R​ρ(U(i+k)​−U(i)​,U(i)​)​(z,w)dw=(i−1)!(k−1)!(n−i−k)!n!​zk−11[0,1]​(z)∫01−z​wi−1(1−z−w)n−i−kdw=(i−1)!(k−1)!(n−i−k)!n!​zk−1(1−z)n−k1[0,1]​(z)∫01​xi−1(1−x)n−i−kdx=(i−1)!(k−1)!(n−i−k)!n!​(n−k)!(i−1)!(n−i−k)!​zk−1(1−z)n−k1[0,1]​(z)=(k−1)!(n−k)!n!​zk−1(1−z)n−k1[0,1]​(z).Namely U(i+k)​−U(i)​∼Beta(k,n−k+1).

(4) Take i=1 and k=n−1 in problem(3) and we know that U(n)​−U(1)​∼Beta(n−1,2).

Problem 2.2

Population U{1,2,…,N}​, order statistics U(1)​≤U(2)​≤⋯≤U(n)​. Calculate P(U(1)​=k),P(U(n)​=k), and P(U(i)​=k). Further, calculate the joint pmf of U(1)​ and U(n)​.

In addition, let U1​,U2​,…,Un​ be the sample randomly drawn from the population of {1:N} without replacement (n<N). Are the pmfs of Ui​,i=1,2,…,n equal? Calculate E[nn+1​U(n)​−1].

Solution: (1)P(U(1)​=k)=P(U(1)​≥k)−P(U(1)​≥k+1)=(NN−k+1​)n−(NN−k​)n.P(U(n)​=k)=P(U(n)​≤k)−P(U(n)​≤k−1)=(Nk​)n−(Nk−1​)n.P(U(i)​=k)=P(U(i)​≤k)−P(U(i)​≤k−1)=[j=i∑n​Cnj​(Nk​)j(NN−k​)n−j]−[j=i∑n​Cnj​(Nk−1​)j(NN−k+1​)n−j].

For 1≤k≤l≤N, if k=l,P(U(1)​=k,U(n)​=l)​=P(U(1)​=k,U(n)​=k)=P(U(1)​=k,U2​≤k,⋯,Un​≤k)=P(U(1)​=k)P(U2​≤k)⋯P(Un​≤k)=Nnkn−1​.​if k<l,P(U(1)​=k,U(n)​=l)​=P(U(1)​=k, the largest of U2​ to Un​=l)=P(U(1)​=k)P( the largest of U2​ to Un​=l)=N1​[(Nl​)n−1−(Nl−1​)n−1].​The two formulas above show the joint pmf of U(1)​ and U(n)​.

(2) Yes. And E[nn+1​U(n)​−1]=N.

Problem 2.3

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​ is a random sample from the population of uniform distribution U[θ,θ+1], −∞<θ<∞. X(1)​,X(2)​,…,X(n)​ are the order statistics, R=X(n)​−X(1)​ and M=(X(1)​+X(n)​)/2 are the sample range and sample midrange.

Solution: (1)f(x,θ)=I{θ≤x≤θ+1}​,∏f(xi​,θ)=i=1∏n​I{θ≤xi​≤θ+1}​=I{X(1)​≥θ}​I{X(n)​≤θ+1}​.(X(1)​,X(n)​) are sufficient statistics,fX(1)​,X(n)​​=n(n−1)(x(n)​−x(1)​)n−2I{θ≤x(1)​<x(n)​≤θ+1}​.

(2)

fR,M​(r,m)=n(n−1)rn−2I{0≤r≤1,θ+2r​≤m≤θ+1−2r​}​.

(3)fR​(r)=∫fR,M​(r,m)dm=n(n−1)rn−2(1−r)I{0≤r≤1}​≡Beta(n−1,2),which doesn’t involve θ, so it is ancillary.

Problem 2.6

Find minimal sufficient statistics of Normal population N(μ,σ2) with unknown μ and σ2.

Solution: Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;θ),θ=(μ,σ2)T thenf(x1​,⋯,xn​;θ)=k=1∏n​2π​σ1​e−2σ2(xk​−μ)2​=(2π​σ1​e−2σ2μ2​)n⋅e−2σ21​∑k=1n​xk2​+σ2μ​∑k=1n​xk​.Let T(X)=(∑k=1n​xk2​,∑k=1n​xk​)T, then T(X) is sufficient statistic for (μ,σ2)T.

Sincef(y;θ)f(x;θ)​=e−2σ21​∑k=1n​(xk2​−yk2​)+σ2μ​∑k=1n​(xk​−yk​),f(y;θ)f(x;θ)​ is independent of (μ,σ2)T iff ∑k=1n​(xk​−yk​)=∑k=1n​(xk2​−yk2​)=0, which is T(x)=T(y).

Thus T(X)=(∑k=1n​xk2​,∑k=1n​xk​)T is a minimal sufficient statistic of θ=(μ,σ2)T.

(Xˉ,S2) can also be regarded as the minimal sufficient statistic of θ=(μ,σ2)T.

Problem 2.7

Find minimal sufficient statistics of

(1) Population: Exponential (λ)

(2) Population: θ+ Exponential (λ) with unknown θ and λ.

Solution: (1) Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;λ), thenf(x;λ)=k=1∏n​λe−λxk​1{xk​>0}​.Let T(X)=∑k=1n​Xk​, then T(X) is a sufficient statistic of λ. Sincef(y;λ)f(x;λ)​=e−λ∑k=1n​(xk​−yk​)1{y1​>0,y2​>0,⋯,yn​>0}​1{x1​>0,x2​>0,⋯,xn​>0}​​,f(y;λ)f(x;λ)​ is independent of λ iff ∑k=1n​(xk​−yk​)=0, which is T(x)=T(y). Thus T(X)=∑k=1n​Xk​ is a minimal sufficient statistic of λ. (Xˉ is also right.)

(2) Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;(θ,λ)T), thenf(x1​,⋯,xn​;(θ,λ)T)=k=1∏n​λe−λ(xk​−θ)1{xk​>θ}​=λnenλθ−λ∑k=1n​xk​1{x1​>θ,x2​>θ,⋯,xn​>θ}​.Let T(X)=(∑k=1n​Xk​,X(1)​)T, then T(X) is a sufficient statistic of (θ,λ)T.

Sincef(y;(θ,λ)T)f(x;(θ,λ)T)​=e−λ∑k=1n​(xk​−yk​)1{y(1)​>θ}​1{x(1)​>θ}​​,f(y;(θ,λ)T)f(x;(θ,λ)T)​ is independent of (θ,λ)T iff ∑k=1n​(xk​−yk​)=x(1)​−y(1)​=0, which is T(x)=T(y).

Thus T(X)=(∑k=1n​Xk​,X(1)​)T is a minimal sufficient statistic of (θ,λ)T.

Problem 2.9

Verify: Family of Poisson (λ), λ>0 distribution is complete.

Solution: If Eλ​(g(X))=∑k=0∞​g(k)k!λk​e−λ=0 for all λ>0, thenh(λ)=k=0∑∞​g(k)k!λk​=0for all λ>0.

Letf(λ)=x=0∑∞​x!g(x)​λx,and f([0,∞))≡0, we take derivatives of f(λ) and can getx!g(x)​=f(x)(λ)x!1​=0∀x≥0thus g(X)≡0, the distribution is complete.

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​∼iidpmf:θ(1−θ)k−1,θ∈(0,1),k=1,2,3,…. Show that ∑i=1n​Xi​ is sufficient for θ, and find the family of distribution of ∑i=1n​Xi​. Is the family complete?

Solution: Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;θ), thenf(x1​,⋯,xn​;θ)=k=1∏n​θ(1−θ)xk​−11{xk​∈Z+​}​=θn(1−θ)−n(1−θ)∑k=1n​xk​1{xk​∈Z+​,k=1,2,⋯,n}​.So let T(X)=∑k=1n​Xk​, then T(X) is sufficient for θ.

f(t;θ)=x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​=t∑​f(x1​,⋯,xn​;θ)=x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​=t∑​θn(1−θ)t−n1{xk​∈Z+​,k=1,2,⋯,n}​=Ct−1n−1​θn(1−θ)t−n.If Eθ​(g(T))=∑t=n∞​g(t)Ct−1n−1​θn(1−θ)t−n for all θ, then h(θ)=∑t=n∞​g(t)Ct−1n−1​(1−θ)t−n=0 for all θ. Since g(t)=(t−n)!Ct−1n−1​1​limθ→0+​h(t−n)(θ)=0,t=n,n+1,⋯. We know the family is complete.

Problem 2.11

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​∼iidpdf:θxθ−1,x∈(0,1),θ>0.

(1) Is ∑i=1n​Xi​ sufficient for θ ?

(2) Find a complete sufficient statistic for θ.

Solution: (1) Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;θ), thenf(x1​,⋯,xn​;θ)=k=1∏n​θxkθ−1​1{0<xk​<1}​=θn(k=1∏n​xk​)θ−11{0<x(1)​<x(n)​<1}​.It is easy to see that ∑k=1n​Xk​ is not sufficient for θ.

(2) Let T(X)=∏k=1n​Xk​, then T(X) is a sufficient statistic for θ. Let Yk​=∏i=1k​Xi​,k=1,2,⋯,n, thenfY​(y1​,y2​,⋯,yn​;θ)​=y1​y2​⋯yn−1​1​fX​(y1​,y1​y2​​,⋯,yn−1​yn​​;θ)=y1​y2​⋯yn−1​1​θnynθ−1​1{0<yn​<yn−1​<⋯<y1​<1}​.​f(t;θ)​=∫fY​(y1​,y2​,⋯,yn−1​,t;θ)dy1​dy2​⋯dyn−1​=∫y1​y2​⋯yn−1​1​θntθ−11{0<t<yn−1​<⋯<y1​<1}​dy1​dy2​⋯dyn−1​=θntθ−1∫1{0<t,lnt<zn−1​<⋯<z1​<0}​dz1​dz2​⋯dzn−1​=θntθ−1(n−1)!(−lnt)n−1​1{0<t<1}​.​IfEθ​(g(T))​=∫01​g(t)θntθ−1(n−1)!(−lnt)n−1​dt=(n−1)!θn​∫0∞​g(e−s)sn−1e−sθds=0​is true for every θ, with Laplace transformation, we have g(e−s)sn−1=0 a.e., which means T(X)=∏k=1n​Xk​ is complete.

Problem 2.12

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​∼iidU(θ,2θ). Find a minimal sufficient statistic for θ. Is the statistic complete?

Solution: Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;θ), thenf(x1​,⋯,xn​;θ)=k=1∏n​θ1​1{θ<xk​<2θ}​=θn1​1{θ<x(1)​,x(n)​<2θ}​.Let T(X)=(X(1)​,X(n)​)T, then T(X) is a sufficient statistic of θ. Since f(y;θ)f(x;θ)​=1{θ<y(1)​,y(n)​<2θ}​1{θ<x(1)​,x(n)​<2θ}​​, f(y;θ)f(x;θ)​ is independent of θ iff x(1)​−y(1)​=x(n)​−y(n)​=0, which is T(x)=T(y).

Thus T(X)=(X(1)​,X(n)​)T is a minimal sufficient statistic for θ.

f(t;θ)=n(n−1)(θ1​)2(θt2​−t1​​)n−21{θ<t1​<t2​<2θ}​.IfEθ​(g(T))=∫g(t)f(t;θ)dt=∫g(t)n(n−1)(θ1​)2(θt2​−t1​​)n−21{θ<t1​<t2​<2θ}​dt1​dt2​=0,equivalently, ∫g(t)(t2​−t1​)n−21{θ<t1​<t2​<2θ}​dt1​dt2​=0.

Let g(t1​,t2​)=(t2​−t1​1​)n−21{t1​<t2​<kt1​}​−(t2​−t1​1​)n−21{kt1​<t2​<2t1​}​ where k=49−17​​, then∫g(t)(t2​−t1​)n−21{θ<t1​<t2​<2θ}​dt1​dt2​≡0thus T is not complete.

Problem 2.13

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​∼iidGamma(α,β), where α is known, then for T=∑1≤i≤n​Xi​E(X(i)​∣T)=E[TX(i)​​T∣T]=TETE[X(i)​]​.

Solution: Suppose X=(X1​,⋯,Xn​)T∼f(x;β), thenf(x1​,⋯,xn​;β)​=k=1∏n​βαΓ(α)1​xkα−1​e−βxk​​1{xk​>0}​=(βαΓ(α)1​)n(k=1∏n​xk​)α−1e−β1​∑k=1n​xk​1{x(1)​>0}​.​Let T(X)=∑k=1n​Xk​, then T(X) is a sufficient statistic of β. By semi-generation of Gamma distribution, we have T∼Gamma(nα,β).

IfEβ​(g(T))=∫g(t)f(t;β)dt=∫g(t)βnαΓ(nα)1​tnα−1e−βt​1{t>0}​dt=0,∀βthen∫0∞​g(t)tnα−1e−βt​dt=0∀β.By Laplace transformation, we have g(t)tnα−1=0 a.e., which means g(t)=0 a.e.. Thus T is complete.

Since βX1​​,βX2​​,⋯,βXn​​∼Gamma(α,1), TX(i)​​=∑k=1n​βXk​​βX(i)​​​ is ancillary statistic. By Basu’s Theorem, we have T is independent of TX(i)​​. ThusE(X(i)​∣T)​=E(TX(i)​​T∣T)=TE(TX(i)​​∣T)=TE(TX(i)​​)=TETE(TX(i)​​)ET​=TETE(X(i)​)​.​

Problem 3.1

XYεX​​=Gγ+g(U)+εX​=Xβ+h(U)+εY​⊥⊥εY​;{U,εX​,εY​}⊥⊥G (IV: Instrumental Variable)​(1) Check β=Cov(Y,G)/Cov(X,G); (2) If we have a realization of triple (G,X,Y) for n individuals, i.e. (Gi​,Xi​,Yi​), i=1,2,…,n, what is the estimator of causal effect β ?

Solution: (1)Cov(Y,G)​=E[YG]−EY⋅EG=βE[XG]+EG⋅Eh(U)+EG⋅EεY​−(βEX+Eh(U)+EεY​)⋅EG=β(E[XG]−EX⋅EG)=βCov(X,G).​Thus β=Cov(X,G)Cov(Y,G)​.

(2)β=n∑i=1n​Xi​Gi​−(∑i=1n​Xi​)(∑i=1n​Gi​)n∑i=1n​Yi​Gi​−(∑i=1n​Yi​)(∑i=1n​Gi​)​.

Problem 3.5: Find MLE

For population: (1) μ+ exponential (θ), i.e. θ1​exp(−θx−μ​)I{x>μ}​,θ>0; (2) kθ1​I{θ<x<(k+1)θ}​, unknown positive θ and known positive k; (3) 2θ1​exp(−θ∣x∣​) with unknown positive θ; (4) I{θ−21​<x<θ+21​}​ (5) θ2​−θ1​1​I{θ1​<x<θ2​}​ with unknown θ1​ and θ2​.

Solution: 1.L(θ,μ)=θn1​exp{−θ1​(i=1∑n​Xi​−nμ)}⋅1{X(1)​>μ}​.For any fixed θ, μ^​MLE​=X(1)​ to insure L(θ,μ) attains its maximum. The log-likelihood functionl(θ)=logL(θ)=−θ1​(i=1∑n​Xi​−nμ)−nlogθ.Let l˙(θ0​)=0, we get θ0​=Xˉ−X(1)​. Check that l¨(θ0​)=−(Xˉ−X(1)​)2n​<0. Thus θ^MLE​=Xˉ−X(1)​,μ^​MLE​=X(1)​.

2.L(θ)=(kθ)n1​1{θ<X(1)​<X(n)​<(k+1)θ}​.Thus θ^MLE​=k+1X(n)​​.

3.L(θ)=(2θ)n1​exp{−θ1​i=1∑n​∣Xi​∣}.The log-likelihood functionl(θ)=logL(θ)=−θ1​i=1∑n​∣Xi​∣−nlogθ+constant.Let l˙(θ0​)=0, we get θ0​=n∑i=1n​∣Xi​∣​. Check that l¨(θ0​)=−θ03​∑i=1n​∣Xi​∣​<0. Thus θ^MLE​=n∑i=1n​∣Xi​∣​.

4.L(θ)=1{θ−21​<X(1)​<X(n)​<θ+21​}​.Thus θ^MLE​=(X(n)​−21​,X(1)​+21​).

5.L(θ)=(θ2​−θ1​)n1​⋅1{θ1​<X(1)​<X(n)​<θ2​}​.Thus θ^1MLE​=X(1)​,θ^2MLE​=X(n)​.

Problem 3.6

(1) Assume X1​∼ Exponential (λ1​) and X2​∼ Exponential (λ2​), and they are independent. Define X=min{X1​,X2​} and Y=I{X=X1​}​. Calculate the joint distribution P{X≤x,Y=0} and P{X≤x,Y=1}. (2) For a random sample (X1​,Y1​),(X2​,Y2​),…,(Xn​,Yn​) from (X,Y) shown in (1), calculate the MLEs of λ1​ and λ2​.

Solution: Let Y1​=X1​−X2​,Y2​=X2​. The joint pdf of (Y1​,Y2​) isρ(y1​,y2​)=λ1​λ2​e−λ1​y1​e−(λ1​+λ2​)y2​⋅1{y1​>0,y1​+y2​>0}​.ThereforeP(X≤x,Y=0)​=P(Y1​>0,Y2​≤x)=λ1​λ2​∫0x​∫0∞​e−λ1​y1​e−(λ1​+λ2​)y2​dy1​dy2​=λ1​+λ2​λ2​​(1−e−(λ1​+λ2​)x)​For the same reason, P(X≤x,Y=1)=λ1​+λ2​λ1​​(1−e−(λ1​+λ2​)x).

(2) Random sample (Xi​,Yi​),i=1,2,…,n. Suppose the number of Y=1 of samples is m, i.e. m=∑i=1n​Yi​.L(λ1​,λ2​)=λ2m​λ1n−m​exp{−(λ1​+λ2​)i=1∑n​Xi​}.The log-likelihood functionl(θ)=logL(θ)=mlogλ2​+(n−m)logλ1​−(λ1​+λ2​)i=1∑n​Xi​.Let ∂λ1​∂l​=0, ∂λ2​∂l​=0. We getλ1​=∑i=1n​Xi​n−m​,λ2​=∑i=1n​Xi​m​.Check that ∂λ1​∂λ2​∂2l​=−diag(λ12​n−m​,λ22​m​) is negative. Thereforeλ^1MLE​=∑i=1n​Xi​n−∑i=1n​Yi​​,λ^2MLE​=∑i=1n​Xi​∑i=1n​Yi​​.

Problem 3.7

A random sample from normal population N(μ,σ2). Write the likelihood function ℓ(μ,σ2), and for any fixed μ, find σ2(μ)=argmaxσ2​ℓ(μ,σ2) and then ℓp​(μ) and μ^​=argmaxμ​ℓp​(μ).

Problem 3.12

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​ is a simple random sample from N(μ,σ2), and let A=n−11​∑i=1n​(Xi​−Xˉ)2,B=n1​∑i=1n​(Xi​−Xˉ)2, C=n+11​∑i=1n​(Xi​−Xˉ)2. Based on MSE (mean squared error) criterion, which one is the best for estimating σ2 ?

Solution:MSE(A)=n−12​σ4,MSE(B)=n22n−1​σ4,MSE(C)=n+12​σ4.Among them the minimal is MSE(C), thereby C=n+11​∑i=1n​(Xi​−Xˉ)2 is best for estimating σ2.

Problem 3.13

Assume X1​,X2​,…,Xn​ is a simple random sample from U(0,θ), and we already know that MLE of θ is θ^mle​=X(n)​ (it is also sufficient for θ), the moment estimator 2Xˉ of θ, and the unbiased estimator nn+1​X(n)​ of θ. Which one do you prefer based on MSE? Further, find a constant c such that MSE[cX(n)​]<MSE[nn+1​X(n)​] for all θ,n>1.

Solution:EX(n)​=n+1n​θ,E[X(n)2​]=n+2n​θ2.MSE(X(n)​)=(n+2)(n+1)2​θ2,MSE(2Xˉ)=n4​Var(X1​)=3n1​θ2,MSE(nn+1​X(n)​)=n2(n+1)2​Var(X(n)​)=n(n+2)1​θ2.Thus, for n>1, nn+1​X(n)​ is better based on MSE.

c=n+1n+2​.

Problem 3.14

(1) For given n pairs of (xi​,yi​),i=1,…,n, let (a,b)=argmina,b​∑i=1n​(yi​−a−bxi​)2, then b=∑i=1n​(xi​−xˉ)2∑i=1n​(xi​−xˉ)yi​​,a=yˉ​−bxˉ, where xˉ=n1​∑i=1n​xi​,yˉ​=n1​∑i=1n​yi​. We call y=a+bx the best line to fit {(xi​,yi​),1≤i≤n}. Check the validity of a and b.

(2) Yi​=β0​+β1​xi​+ϵi​,ϵ1​,ϵ2​,…,ϵn​∼iidN(0,σ2),x1​,x2​,…,xn​ are fixed constants. β0​,β1​, and σ2 are unknown parameters of interest.

(i) Check (∑i=1n​Yi​,∑i=1n​xi​Yi​,∑i=1n​Yi2​) is sufficient for the unknown parameters.

(ii) Find the MLEs of unknown parameters and judge if it is unbiased.

(iii) Find the distributions of MLEs.

Solution: (1)L(a,b):=i=1∑n​(yi​−a−bxi​)2.Let ∂a∂L​=0,∂b∂L​=0. We geta^=yˉ​−b^xˉ,b^=∑i=1n​(xi​−xˉ)2∑i=1n​(xi​−xˉ)yi​​.Check that∂a∂b∂2L​=(n∑i=1n​xi​​∑i=1n​xi​∑i=1n​xi2​​)which is nonnegative. Thus (a^,b^)=argmina,b​∑i=1n​(yi​−a−bxi​)2.

(2) Yi​=β0​+β1​xi​+ϵi​,ϵi​∼N(0,σ2) i.i.d..

(i) Yi​∼N(β0​+β1​xi​,σ2) independently. Therefore the joint pdf of y=(y1​,…,yn​) isf(y)=(2πσ2)−2n​⋅exp{−2σ21​i=1∑n​(yi​−β0​−β1​xi​)2}.Considering ∑i=1n​(yi​−β0​−β1​xi​)2=∑i=1n​Yi2​+∑i=1n​(β0​+β1​xi​)2−2∑i=1n​Yi​(β0​+β1​xi​), by the factorization theorem, (∑i=1n​Yi​,∑i=1n​xi​Yi​,∑i=1n​Yi2​) is sufficient for the unknown parameters.

(ii) & (iii): Considering the matrix version of this problem we haveβ^​=(β^​1​,β^​0​)T=(XTX)−1XTywhere X=⎝⎛​x1​x2​⋮xn​​11⋮1​⎠⎞​n×2​. Thus β^​ is unbiased.

Let G=X(XTX)−1XT, then σ^2=nyT(I−G)y​∼nσ2​χ2(n−2). Thus σ^2 is unbiased.

Problem 3.15

Population: θxθ−1I{0<x<1}​,θ>0.

(1) Find the MLE of θ1​;

(2) Find the efficient estimator of θ1​.

Solution: (1) l(θ)=∑i=1n​((θ−1)lnXi​+lnθ)=nlnθ+(∑i=1n​lnXi​)θ−∑i=1n​lnXi​. Thus θ^mle​=−∑i=1n​lnXi​n​, and(θ^1​)mle​=θ^mle​1​=−n1​i=1∑n​lnXi​.

(2) Let S=−n1​∑i=1n​lnXi​∈(0,+∞), then S∼(n−1)!(nθ)n​e−nθssn−1ds.ES=∫0+∞​s(n−1)!(nθ)n​e−nθssn−1ds=n!θ1​∫0+∞​e−ttndt=θ1​.Therefore S is an unbiased estimator of θ1​.ES2=∫0+∞​s2(n−1)!(nθ)n​e−nθssn−1ds=n⋅n!θ21​∫0+∞​e−ttn+1dt=nθ2n+1​,Var(S)=ES2−(ES)2=nθ21​.i(θ1​)=E[(−θ2lnx−θ)2]=∫01​θxθ−1(θ2lnx+θ)2dx=θ2,I(θ1​)=ni(θ1​)=nθ2.Thus Var(S)=nθ21​=I(θ1​)1​, so S=−n1​∑i=1n​lnXi​ is the efficient estimator of θ1​.

Problem 3.16

Population: Gamma (α,β),α>0 is known. Prove that Xˉ/α is efficient for β.

Solution: We knowE[Gamma(α,β)]=αβ,Var(Gamma(α,β))=αβ2.The log-likelihood functionl(β)=−nlog(Γ(α)βα)+(α−1)i=1∑n​logXi​−β1​i=1∑n​Xi​.l˙(β)=−βαn​+β2∑i=1n​Xi​​,l¨(β)=β2αn​−β32∑i=1n​Xi​​.Check thatE(αXˉ​)=α1​E(Gamma(α,β))=β,Var(αXˉ​)=α2Var(Xˉ)​=αnβ2​.E(−l¨(β))=−β2αn​+β32n​E(Gamma(α,β))=β2αn​.Thus αXˉ​ is unbiased and satisfies Var(αXˉ​)=I(β)1​.

Problem 3.17

Population U[0,θ], Sample X1​,…,Xn​. Find MVUE of unknown parameter θ.

Solution: Population: U[0,θ]. Let T=nn+1​X(n)​. ThenET=∫0θ​nn+1​x⋅nθn1​xn−1dx=θ,thus T is unbiased. Besides, for any θ, if g(x) satisfies∫0θ​g(x)θnn​xn−1dx≡0.Then, by taking derivatives,−∫0θ​g(x)θn+1n2​xn−1dx+θn​g(θ)≡0.Thus g(x)≡0, then X(n)​ is complete.

We also know that X(n)​ is sufficient. So by Theorem 3.6, T=nn+1​X(n)​ is the unique MVUE of θ.

Problem 3.18

Population: Poisson (λ)

(1) Calculate the Fisher information i(λ1​);

(2) Find one function g(λ) such that i[g(λ)] does not dependent on λ.

Solution: Population: Poisson (λ). (1) The log-likelihood functionl(λ)=−nλ1​−i=1∑n​Xi​⋅logλ1​.∂λ1​∂l​=λ(nλ−i=1∑n​Xi​).ThusI(λ1​)=E[(∂λ1​∂l​)2]=nλ3,i(λ1​)=n1​I(λ1​)=λ3.

(2) g(λ)=λ​ is desired.l(λ)=−n(λ​)2+2i=1∑n​Xi​⋅logλ​.Then∂λ​2∂2l​=−2n−λ​22∑i=1n​Xi​​.i(λ​)=n1​E(∂λ​2∂2l​)=4.Therefore, i(g(λ)) does not depend on λ.

Problem 3.19

Population: N(μ,1). Find the MVUE of μ2 and prove that its variance is bigger that the CRLB.

Solution:l(μ)=−21​i=1∑n​Xi2​+i=1∑n​Xi​⋅μ2​−2n​μ2−2n​log2π.We can derive thatI(μ2)=E[(∂μ2)2∂2l​]=4μ2n​.With factorization theorem, we know that T=n∑i=1n​Xi​​ is sufficient, and T∼N(μ,n1​). By Laplace transformation, we can get N(μ,n1​) is complete. Now let g(x)=x2−n1​. Then g(T) is an unbiased estimator. So g(T) is MVUE of μ2. Now let X=n​(T−μ). Then X2∼χ2(1), thus Var(X2)=2. SoVar((T−μ)2)=n2​.We getVar(g(T))=Var(T2)=n2​+n4μ2​which is strictly bigger than CRLB.

Problem 3.20

Two independent samples X1​,X2​,…,Xn​∼iidN(μ,σ2) and Y1​,Y2​,…,Yn​∼iidN(μ,2σ2). Find the MVUE of μ and σ2, respectively.

Solution: For X, we have done in class. μ^​X​=Xˉ,σ2^X​=S2. For Y,μ^​Y​=Yˉ,σ^Y2​=21​S2.f(y;μ,2σ2)=4πσ2​1​exp(−4σ21​(y−μ)2),l(μ,σ2)=−21​log2π−21​log2σ2−4σ21​(y−μ)2.ThenEμ^​Y​=EYˉ=μ;Eσ2^Y​=21​ES2=σ2;Varμ^​Y​=n1​VarY=n2σ2​;Varσ^Y2​=Var2σ2(n−1)S2​=n−12​σ4.Besides,l˙(μ)=2σ21​(Y−μ);I(μ)=2σ2n​;l˙(σ2)=2σ21​[(2​σY−μ​)2−1];I(σ2)=2σ4n​,which shows that MVUE is no smaller than CRLB.

Problem 3.21

Population: Exponential (θ). We know that the sample mean is the moment estimator, MLE, sufficient, and consistent, and also MVUE (cf. Example 3.7). Prove that there exists θ^ such MSE(θ^)<MSE(Xˉ). (Hint: consider cXˉ).

Solution:MSE(cXˉ)​=E(cXˉ−θ)2=E(c2(Xˉ)2−2cθXˉ+θ2)=n2c2​E(X1​+⋯+Xn​)2−n2cθ​nθ+θ2=n2c2​(2nθ2+(n2−n)θ2)−2cθ2+θ2=(nn+1​c2−2c+1)θ2.​Let c=1,n+1n​, thenMSE(Xˉ)=nθ2​,MSE(θ^)=n+1θ2​.Thus, θ^=n+1n​Xˉ satisfies the requirement.

Problem 3.23

Population: Exponential(λ)=Gamma(1,λ). Find the 1−α CI for λ; Population: θ+Exponential(1). Find the 1−α CI for θ.

Solution: X∼Gamma(1,λ), Y:=λX​, thenρY​(y)=ρX​(λy)λ=e−y⋅1(0,∞)​(y).Thus CDF of Y is F(y)=1−e−y. Let y1​,y2​ solutions of F(y1​)=2α​,F(y2​)=1−2α​, respectively. Then y1​=−log(1−2α​),y2​=−log(2α​). We haveP(y1​≤Y≤y2​)=1−α,P(y2​X​≤λ≤y1​X​)=1−α.

Problem 3.24

Population: U(θ−21​,θ+21​). Prove 2X(1)​+X(n)​​−θ is a pivot and then find the 1−α CI for θ.

Solution: Let X∼U(θ−21​,θ+21​),Y=X−θ. Then Y∼U(−21​,21​). Note that 2X(1)​+X(n)​​−θ=2Y(1)​+Y(n)​​ which is independent of θ, Thus 2X(1)​+X(n)​​−θ is a pivot. Let P(a≤2Y(1)​+Y(n)​​≤b)=1−α, ThenP(2X(1)​+X(n)​​−b≤θ≤2X(1)​+X(n)​​−a)=1−α.

Problem 3.25

Population: U(θ1​,θ2​). Find the 1−α CIs for θ2​−θ1​ and 2θ1​+θ2​​, respectively.

Solution: Let Y1​=X(n)​−X(1)​,Y2​=X(n)​. We can getP(X(1)​≤x1​,X(n)​≤x2​)=(θ2​−θ1​)n(x2​−θ1​)n−(x2​−x1​)n​.The joint pdf of (X(1)​,X(n)​) isρX​(x1​,x2​)=(θ2​−θ1​)nn(n−1)​(x2​−x1​)n−21{θ1​≤x1​≤x2​≤θ2​}​(x1​,x2​).ρY​(y1​,y2​)=ρX​(y2​−y1​,y2​)=(θ2​−θ1​)nn(n−1)​y1n−2​⋅1{0≤y1​,y1​+θ1​≤y2​≤θ2​}​.Thus marginal pdf of Y1​ isρ(y1​)=∫y1​+θ1​θ2​​ρY​(y1​,y2​)dy2​=(θ2​−θ1​)n−1n(n−1)​y1n−2​(1−θ2​−θ1​y1​​).Then pdf of X isf(x)=θ2​−θ1​1​ρ(θ2​−θ1​x​)=n(n−1)xn−2(1−x)⋅1(0,1)​(x).Then θ2​−θ1​X(n)​−X(1)​​∼Beta(n−1,2). The 1−α C.I. for θ2​−θ1​ satisfies1−α=P{L≤θ2​−θ1​≤U}=P{UX(n)​−X(1)​​≤θ2​−θ1​X(n)​−X(1)​​≤LX(n)​−X(1)​​}that is(UX(n)​−X(1)​​,LX(n)​−X(1)​​)=(Beta2α​​(n−1,2),Beta1−2α​​(n−1,2)),(L,U)=(Beta1−2α​​(n−1,2)X(n)​−X(1)​​,Beta2α​​(n−1,2)X(n)​−X(1)​​).

(2) Letu=X(n)​−X(1)​X(1)​+X(n)​−(θ1​+θ2​)​,v=X(n)​−X(1)​.Then the joint pdf of (X(1)​,X(n)​) isf(x,y)=(θ2​−θ1​)nn(n−1)​(y−x)n−21{θ1​≤x≤y≤θ2​}​,so the joint pdf of (u,v) isl(u,v)=f(2uv+θ1​+θ2​−v​,2uv+v+θ1​+θ2​​)2∣v∣​.Thusl(u,v)=2(θ2​−θ1​)nn(n−1)vn−1​1{θ1​≤2uv+θ1​+θ2​−v​≤2uv+v+θ1​+θ2​​≤θ2​}​.Thus the pdf of U isf(u)=∫l(u,v)dv=2(θ2​−θ1​)nn(n−1)​(1{u≥0}​∫01+uθ1​+θ2​​​vn−1dv+1{u≤0}​∫01−uθ2​−θ1​​​vn−1dv)=2(1+∣u∣)nn−1​.The 1−α C.I. for 2θ1​+θ2​​ satisfies2α​=∫t∞​2(1+u)nn−1​du=2(1+t)−(n−1)​,then t=α−n−11​−1. We need1−α=P{L≤θ1​+θ2​≤U}=P{X(n)​−X(1)​X(1)​+X(n)​−U​≤X(n)​−X(1)​X(1)​+X(n)​−(θ1​+θ2​)​≤X(n)​−X(1)​X(1)​+X(n)​−L​}that is(L,U)=(X(1)​+X(n)​−(X(n)​−X(1)​)(α−n−11​−1),X(1)​+X(n)​+(X(n)​−X(1)​)(α−n−11​−1)).

Problem 3.26

Two independent samples X1​,X2​,…,Xm​∼iidU(0,θ1​) and Y1​,Y2​,…,Yn​∼iidU(0,θ2​). Find the 1−α CI for θ2​θ1​​. (Hint: consider Y(n)​X(m)​​)

Solution: Let T1​=X(m)​,T2​=Y(n)​, then X=θ1​T1​​∼B(m,1),Y=θ2​T2​​∼B(n,1). Thus, T=YX​ is a pivot. The pdf of T isf(t)f(t)​=m+nmn​tm−1,0<t<1;=m+nmn​t−n−1,t≥1.​Then the 1−α C.I. for θ2​θ1​​ is[Y(n)​X(m)​​(mm+n​2α​)n1​,Y(n)​X(m)​​(nm+n​2α​)−m1​].

Problem 3.27

For population: Bernoulli (p), we already know that T=∑i=1n​Xi​∼Binomial(n,p) is sufficient for p.

(1) Use integration by parts or differentiation both sides with respect to p to prove P{Binomial(n,p)≥k}=P{Beta(k,n−k+1)≤p}.

(3) Prove the 1−α CI for p is[T+(n−T+1)F1−2α​​(2n−2T+2,2T)T​,(n−T)+(T+1)F1−2α​​(2T+2,2n−2T)(T+1)F1−2α​​(2T+2,2n−2T)​].Hint. Use property of F distribution. cf. Homework 1.5, page 27.

Solution: (1) Same as Problem 1.6.

(2) P{Beta(k,n−k+1)≤p}=P{Beta(n−k+1,k)≥1−p}, and Fα​(m,n)=F1−α​(n,m)1​.

By changing variables,P{Beta(k,n−k+1)≤p}​=∫0p​B(k,n−k+1)1​xk−1(1−x)n−kdx=∫1−p1​B(n−k+1,k)1​(1−x)k−1xn−kdx=P{Beta(n−k+1,k)≥1−p}.​

Let F∼F(m,n), by definition,α=P{F<Fα​(m,n)}=P{F1​>Fα​(m,n)1​}.Note that F1​∼F(n,m), thusα=P{F1​>F1−α​(n,m)}.ThusFα​(m,n)=F1−α​(n,m)1​.

(3) The CDF of T isG(t,p)=Pp​(T≤t)=i=1∑[t]​Cni​pi(1−p)n−i=Γ(k+1)Γ(n−k)Γ(n+1)​∫p1​uk(1−u)n−iduwhere [t]=k. G(t,p) is continuous and strictly decreasing for p. Let T=k,i=0∑k−1​Cni​pi(1−p)n−i=1−2α​that isΓ(k−1)Γ(n−k+1)Γ(n+1)​∫0p​uk−1(1−u)n−kdu=2α​.Note that if B∼Beta(m,n), then F=1−BB​mn​∼F(2m,2n). Here F=1−pp​kn−k+1​∼F(2k,2(n−k+1)). Let1−pp​kn−k+1​=Fα/2​(2k,2(n−k+1)).We use T to denote k, thuspl​=kFα/2​+(n−k+1)kFα/2​​=T+(n−k+1)F1−α/2​(2(n−k+1),2k)T​.For pu​, leti=0∑k​Cni​pi(1−p)n−i=2α​.Note that1−pp​k+1n−k​∼F(2(k+1),2(n−k)),then 1−pp​k+1n−k​=F1−α/2​(2(k+1),2(n−k)). We use T to denote k, thuspu​=(n−k)+(k+1)F1−α/2​(2(k+1),2(n−k))(T+1)F1−α/2​(2(k+1),2(n−k))​.

Two independent samples from normal populations N(μX​,σX2​) and N(μY​,σY2​), respectively.

Problem 4.7

For the simple null hypothesis H0​:θ=θ0​, verify p(X)∼U(0,1) under H0​, where p(x)=inf{α∈(0,1)∣φα​(x)=1},Eθ0​​[φα​(X)]=α, φα​ is a non-randomized test function (i.e., φα​(x)∈{0,1} for all x),{x:φα1​​(x)=1}⊆{x:φα2​​(x)=1} when α1​<α2​.

Solution: α=Eθ0​​[φα​(X)]=Pθ0​​(φα​(X)=1)

p(x)<α⇒φα​(x)=1⇒p(x)≤α

Pθ0​​(p(X)<α)≤Pθ0​​(φα​(X)=1)=α≤Pθ0​​(p(X)≤α),∀α∈(0,1)

P(Y<α)≤α≤P(Y≤α)

If P(Y=β)=r>0,

β+ε≥P(Y<β+ε)≥P(Y≤β−δ)+P(Y=β)≥β−δ+r

Let ε,δ>0,ε+δ<r. The contradiction was derived.

Problem 4.12

Let G1​,⋯,GM​ be the genotypes of an individual at loci 1∼M, respectively, and D be his/her affection status, i.e. D=1 means affected and D=0 means unaffected.

The logistic regression model is

logitP(D=1∣G1​,⋯,GM​)=β0​+G1​β1​+⋯+GM​βM​.

Now we collect the genotypes and phenotypes for n individuals {(Di​,Gi1​,⋯,GiM​)∣i=1,2,⋯,n}. Derive the Score test statistic about the null hypothesis of no association between M-locus genotype and phenotype H0​:β1​=⋯=βM​=0.

25 春, 25 秋 (yy)

25 秋考试范围:

1. 统计量: 充分统计量-因子分解定理, 极小充分统计量, (关于分布族的) 完备统计量, Basu 定理, 指数型分布族

2. 点估计-无偏性准则: 均方误差 (MSE), 一致最小方差无偏估计 (UMVUE), Fisher 信息矩阵, 无偏估计的 Cramer-Rao 下界

待估参数 g(θ) 的 UMVUE 的 3 种求解方法:

(a) 求出 θ 的一个完备充分统计量 T 之后, 待定可测函数 h 使得 Eθ​[h(T(X))]=g(θ)

(b) 求出 θ 的一个完备充分统计量 T 与 g(θ) 的一个无偏估计 g^​ 之后, 计算条件期望 E[g^​(X)∣T(X)]

(c) 求出 θ 的一个充分统计量 T 之后, 待定可测函数 h 使得 Eθ​[h(T(X))f(T(X))]=0,∀ 可测函数 f s.t. Eθ​[f(T(X))]=0,Eθ​[(f(T(X)))2]<+∞. 如果这样的 h 不存在, 则 UMVUE 不存在 (Based on Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 2.5 (ii) in Mathematical Statistics by Jun Shao)

3. 点估计-估计方法: 矩估计, 极大似然估计 (MLE)

4. 假设检验-参数检验问题-最优势准则:

(1) 假设检验问题的相关基本定义:

(随机化) 检验函数 (简称 “检验” in Jun Shao’s book) 的势函数 (power function)、显著性水平 (level of significance)、检验水准 (size)

非随机化检验的拒绝域、检验统计量

一族以 size α∈(0,1) 为参数的非随机化检验函数 φα​ 相对于给定的 x∈Rn (这里的 n 对应到样本 X 是 n 维随机向量) 的 p-值 p(x):=inf{α∈(0,1)∣φα​(x)=1}

(2) 一致最优势检验 (UMPT): 简单假设检验问题的 UMPT, 单调似然比分布族的单边检验问题的 UMPT, 单参数指数型分布族的一种双边检验问题的 UMPT

(3) 一致最优势无偏检验 (UMPUT): 无偏检验、边界相似检验的定义, 多参数指数型分布族中的结论, 正态分布族中的结论

5. 假设检验-参数检验问题-检验方法:

(1) 似然比检验 (LRT)

(2) (在零假设对应的参数空间维数小于整体参数空间维数时) 似然比统计量的渐近分布, Wald 检验, Rao 得分检验

6. 假设检验-非参数检验问题-检验方法:

(1) 单样本中位数检验问题: Wilcoxon 符号秩检验, 两样本中位数检验问题: Mann-Whitney 检验

(2) 拟合优度检验问题:

(一维连续型分布) Kolmogorov-Smirnov 检验, Cramér-von Mises 检验, Anderson–Darling 检验

(离散型分布) Pearsonχ2 检验, 列联表独立性检验

7. 区域估计:

最精确准则: 一致最精确置信域 (UMA)

估计方法: 反转假设检验问题的拒绝域, 构造枢轴量

—

考试范围之外但上课讲授的内容:

Wald 统计决策理论的基本概念

Bayes 估计与 Minimax 估计的基本概念

大样本理论中的一些结论 (相合性, 强相和性, 渐近分布, 即概率极限理论中的依概率, 几乎必然, 依分布收敛)

线性模型中的最小二乘估计

用 U 统计量构造无偏估计

参考教材:

[1] Mathematical Statistics by Jun Shao

其他可以参考的统计学书籍:

[2] Theory of Point Estimation by Erich Lehmann

[3] Testing Statistical Hypotheses by Erich Lehmann

[4] Mathematical Statistics: Basic Ideas and Selected Topics (Two Volumes) by Peter J. Bickel

[5] 高等统计学. 薛留根

[6] 数理统计引论. 陈希孺

25 秋期末的最后一题: 设参数 r∈(0,+∞), R2 上相对于 Lebesgue 测度的密度函数族为 fr​(x,y)=πr21​1{x2+y2⩽r2}​, 取 n 个相互独立的样本 {(Xi​,Yi​)}i=1n​∼i.i.dfr​(x,y)dxdy.

(1) 求参数 r∈(0,+∞) 的一个完备充分统计量.

答案: 1⩽i⩽nmax​(Xi2​+Yi2​)

(2) 求参数 r 的一个最小方差无偏估计.

答案: 2n2n+1​1⩽i⩽nmax​(Xi2​+Yi2​)​

(3) 求参数 r 的一个置信水平为 1−α 的置信区间.

答案: ⎣⎡​(1−2α​)2n1​1⩽i⩽nmax​(Xi2​+Yi2​)​​,(2α​)2n1​1⩽i⩽nmax​(Xi2​+Yi2​)​​⎦⎤​
